title: The Caliph and the Poet
author: James Baldwin
summary: 诗人为了讨赏选了智慧，哈里发用三句玩笑话抵掉金币，最后仍赏他五百金。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1912 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time there was a famous Arab whose name was Al Mansur. He was the ruler of all the Arabs, and was therefore called the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，有一位著名的阿拉伯人，名叫阿尔·曼苏尔。他是所有阿拉伯人的统治者，因此被称为哈里发。

paragraphs.en: Al Mansur loved poetry and was fond of hearing poets repeat their own verses. Sometimes, if a poem was very pleasing, he gave the poet a prize. One day a poet whose name was Thalibi came to the caliph and recited a long poem. When he had finished, he bowed, and waited, hoping that he would be rewarded.
paragraphs.zh: 阿尔·曼苏尔喜爱诗歌，喜欢听诗人朗诵自己的诗。有时，一首诗若非常动听，他就赏赐诗人。一天，一个名叫萨利比的诗人来到哈里发面前，朗诵了一首长诗。诵完后，他鞠了一躬，等着赏赐。

paragraphs.en: "Which would you rather have" asked the caliph, "three hundred pieces of gold, or three wise sayings from my lips?"
paragraphs.zh: “你更愿意要哪一样？”哈里发问，“三百枚金币，还是我口中的三句至理名言？”

paragraphs.en: The poet wished very much to please the caliph. So he said, "Oh, my master, everybody should choose wisdom rather than wealth."
paragraphs.zh: 诗人很想讨哈里发欢心，便说：“哦，我的主人，人人都该选择智慧，而不是财富。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph smiled, and said, "Very well, then, listen to my first wise saying: When your coat is worn out, don't sew on a new patch; it will look ugly."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发笑了，说：“好吧，那就听我第一句至理名言：外套破了，别缝新补丁，那会很难看。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, dear!" moaned the poet. "There go a hundred gold pieces all at once." The caliph smiled again. Then he said, "Listen now to my second word of wisdom. It is this: When you oil your beard, don't oil it too much, lest it soil your clothing."
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀！”诗人呻吟道，“这一下就没了一百枚金币。”哈里发又笑了笑，说：“现在听我第二句至理名言：给胡子上油时，别上得太多，免得弄脏衣裳。”

paragraphs.en: "Worse and worse!" groaned the poor poet. "There go the second hundred. What shall I do?"
paragraphs.zh: “越来越糟！”可怜的诗人哀叹道，“第二个一百也没了。我可怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: "Wait, and I will tell you," said the caliph; and he smiled again. "My third wise saying is—"
paragraphs.zh: “等着，我这就告诉你，”哈里发说着又笑了，“我的第三句至理名言是——”

paragraphs.en: "O caliph, have mercy!" cried the poet. "Keep the third piece of wisdom for your own use, and let me have the gold."
paragraphs.zh: “哦，哈里发，行行好吧！”诗人叫道，“第三句智慧您自己留着用吧，把金子给我。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph laughed outright, and so did every one that heard him. Then he ordered his treasurer to pay the poet five hundred pieces of gold; for, indeed, the poem which he had recited was wonderfully fine.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发放声大笑，听见的人也都笑了。然后他吩咐司库付给诗人五百枚金币；因为诗人朗诵的那首诗确实精彩极了。

paragraphs.en: The caliph, Al Mansur, lived nearly twelve hundred years ago. He was the builder of a famous and beautiful city called Bagdad.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发阿尔·曼苏尔生活在将近一千二百年前。他建造了一座著名而美丽的城市，名叫巴格达。
